A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work. The main text, algorithms, Table 1, equations, and complete Appendices A-D are readable and can be matched across the layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports algorithms, analytical query-complexity bounds, and proofs. Table 1 specifies a theoretical lower-bound construction; no original experimental, simulation, or data-analysis outcomes are reported.

after.justification: v2 retains the theoretical treatment without empirical evaluation, including in its appendices. The new introductory example involving stochastic simulations provides motivation but reports no simulation outcomes.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 and the threshold-based allocation procedure in Section 4 and Appendix C are retained. Repeated sampling, subsampling when queries are fewer than items, threshold selection, and random allocation of unqueried items are unchanged.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or empirical evaluation tasks. v2 adds motivating scenarios involving stochastic simulations and group-average valuations, but does not train or evaluate on them.

E2.justification: Neither version reports experimentally evaluated comparators. Algorithm 1 remains the same analytically studied reference procedure, and no comparison method is added or removed.

E3.justification: Neither version reports an experimental evaluation protocol. The correction to the theoretical conditions summarized in Section 6 does not change an experimental setting.

E4.justification: No ablations, robustness tests, sensitivity experiments, or case studies are added or removed. The appendix analyses retain the same upper- and lower-bound proofs; the added small-gap discussion concerns interpretation.

E5.justification: The analytical concentration and failure-probability bounds are retained. Neither version reports repeated empirical runs, error bars, or empirical significance tests.

E6.justification: There are no empirical result entries in either version. Table 1 retains identical valuation types, and the query-complexity formulas and numerical constants in the theorem statements and appendix proofs are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 2 replaces the claim that arbitrary valuation intervals can be shifted and rescaled with rescaling intervals of the form [0, u_max]. Section 6 corrects its condition from Δ < 2σ²m to Δ < min{2σ²m, √2 σm}, matching Equation (101), which already appeared in v1. These are limited mathematical corrections; the appendix theorem statements and proofs remain substantively unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution summary, and conclusion retain the same central claims: query complexity scaling as m^(5/2)/Δ² up to logarithmic factors in the stated regime, a polynomial-time nonadaptive upper bound, and a lower bound allowing adaptive queries and arbitrary computation.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies that Section 3's loose guarantee may reflect the analysis rather than an intrinsic limitation of Algorithm 1. Remark 2 adds possible computational barriers for small Δ through NP-hardness of envy-free allocation. The new group-valuation example also explicitly limits fairness to group averages.

D1.justification: The sampling rules, threshold grid, and theoretical parameter choices remain unchanged. Neither version adds implementation instructions, hardware information, or code and data access information.

R1.justification: v2 adds Lipton et al. (2004) to support the computational-hardness discussion. Banihashem et al. and Verma et al. receive publication-reference updates for already cited works. The broader related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: The introduction expands its motivation into three scenarios, and Section 3 and Remark 2 receive localized explanatory additions. v2 also updates affiliations and acknowledgments, adds an Impact Statement, and makes small editorial corrections. The section and appendix organization is retained.

P2.justification: v2 converts the main text and references from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout, with new title formatting and running headers. Algorithm 1 and Table 1 are reformatted and repositioned, and the single-column appendices are extensively reflowed. No figure or table content is added.

improvement.justification: v2 improves mathematical precision by correcting the normalization statement and aligning Section 6 with the condition already present in Theorem 6. It also more carefully distinguishes analytical looseness from algorithmic limitations and explains possible small-gap barriers. These are useful, limited improvements; the central algorithms, guarantees, and appendix proofs remain substantively unchanged.
